newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SGIO expects flat year result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SGIO expects flat year result.

text.p: Perth-based insurance group SGIO Insurance Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to record a flat result in the year to June 30.
The company reported a net profit of A$29.35 million in the year to June 30, 1996.
"I would think our result will be similar to last year," managing director Ian Brown told reporters after a Securities Institute of Australia briefing.

Brown said the company had had a magnificent year in investments, but it was time to take a conservative approach to some of the "long tail classes" like workers compensation or liability insurance where the claims took longer to settle.
"We are starting to see some trends with growth in those areas of claims now," he said.
Brown said he did not expect the current investment markets to remain as bouyant as they had been.
"We are putting more reserves into our outstanding funds," he said, adding that insurance rates could not rise as much as they should with the market currently overserviced.

Brown said that although he believed SGIO had a takeover premium built into its share price, he did not believe it was currently a target, although any offer was more likely to come from overseas than from Australia.

He said the Australian insurance industry needed further rationalisation and SGIO was actively seeking opportunites to expand from its base in Western Australian and South Australia to the eastern states.
Brown said SGIO's expansion strategy was to either buy an established portfolio business or form a relationship or alliance with another player.
He said he hoped to make such a move into health insurance within the next 12 months, and also to establish a joint venture in Asia in the next two to three years.
